(in reference to post above)

I think the general concept is remaining LQ is left over from trapped orders occurring when price fakes out before turning abruptly. All this type of trade is: taking advantage of the 'bounce' from left over orders at a level where there was some previous carnage.

The stronger the false move, and the stronger the move away from that false move, the greater likelihood of a a bounce when price returns to that area.

Also, the false move should break highs or lows to its left (it should be convincing.. because the more convincing the false move, the more trapped LQ remaining at that level.

I am going to keep back testing this to see how frequently we get at least a 3R trade from these trapped LQ zones... also will be trying different TF to see if that makes a difference on the reliability of the trades.

(let's pretend my drawing shows a much stronger sustained move down after the trick... it is getting late here and I don't have the energy to re draw it

hoeschec wrote: (in reference to post above)

I think the general concept is remaining LQ is left over from trapped orders occurring when price fakes out before turning abruptly. All this type of trade is: taking advantage of the 'bounce' from left over orders at a level where there was some previous carnage.

The stronger the false move, and the stronger the move away from that false move, the greater likelihood of a a bounce when price returns to that area.

Also, the false move should break highs or lows to its left (it should be convincing.. because the more convincing the false move, the more trapped LQ remaining at that level.

#1: Traders who are short have SL at this location... those are triggered

#2. Breakout traders go long on break of that bearish FL. They have SL that are hit around point 2

I believe you are spot on in your thinking about residual orders on these types of scenarios. The way I think about it, perhaps incorrectly, is that IT create a false breakout where they trick uninformed traders into buying. The better the trick the more orders they have to overcome to reverse the market. So I figure if they build a really great level that draws lots and lots of interest that means they have to dump more sells to overcome the buyers and drop the market. If they dumped lots of sells onto the market chances are those orders were not all filled because the market moved too fast. So when we come back to revisit the area, those leftover orders are often sitting there waiting to be filled.

The only way this wouldn't be the case is if they pull the unfilled orders. Which I imagine they would only do if the market extended down to their target and it was some type of substantial bullish set-up like a QM or DM on HTF.

posts.t:
I totally agree!

Gregg mentioned a concept to me a few months ago which I have applied to my trading... he uses the term 'square up'. I interpret 'squaring up' as the trapped LQ left over after the main event has occurred... tremendous capital is spent to push price in that false direction, and those open orders remain on their balance sheet as the trade progresses. Since banks and institutional funds don't use SL, they have to 'square up' or clear the orders open and dragging on their balance sheet. When price RT to that false breakout, they get out of these positions...and that is the bounce I trade.

It all seems quite logical to me... and it explains (in part) why these areas are so reactive when price returns.

کاملاً موافقم!

Gregg چند ماه پیش یه مفهومی رو به من گفت که تو معامله‌ام به کار بردم… اون از اصطلاح 'square up' استفاده می‌کنه. من «square up» رو LQ به‌دام‌افتادهٔ باقی‌مونده بعد از رخداد رویداد اصلی تفسیر می‌کنم… سرمایهٔ عظیمی خرج می‌شه تا قیمت رو تو اون جهت کاذب هل بده و اون سفارش‌های باز با پیشرفت معامله رو ترازنامه‌شون باقی می‌مونن. چون بانک‌ها و صندوق‌های نهادی SL استفاده نمی‌کنن، باید 'square up' کنن یا سفارش‌های باز و کشیده‌شده رو از ترازنامه پاک کنن. وقتی قیمت RT به اون بریک‌اوت کاذب می‌کنه، از این موقعیت‌ها خارج می‌شن… و همون جهشیه که من معامله می‌کنم.

همه‌ش برام کاملاً منطقی به نظر می‌رسه… و توضیح می‌ده (تا حدی) چرا این نواحی وقتی قیمت برمی‌گرده این‌قدر واکنش نشون می‌دن.

"The engulf that matters is the one that proceeds a met target in the opposite direction"

hoeschec wrote: I have been doing some research lately... I am pondering the following concept:

"The engulf that matters is the one that proceeds a met target in the opposite direction"

Don't automatically take this as being true....because I am not sure it is....it's just something I've come up with lately that I think may have some significance.

In other words engulf has to be engulf of reaction to a FL. If engulf happens in space, there is possibility of price going against you to true Supply/Demand (FL).

However I think engulf that happens in the space is for future reference. I think at one point in Salivan's journal he said difference between FO and EG is where it happens and FO turns into engulf in future.

dengaima wrote: In other words engulf has to be engulf of reaction to a FL.

I think what H wrote was consistent with what Salivan said in one of his posts: -There is no engulf south unless price has reached its target for long (so target for long means price has reached an UFL) -There is no engulf north unless price has reached its target for short (so target for short means price has reached a LFL)

Astrokillah wrote: Dear Dengaima, I have been reading this sentence many times, and I have failed to understand it, call me stupid, could you draw what you mean? Thanks.

dengaima wrote: In other words engulf has to be engulf of reaction to a FL.

I think what H wrote was consistent with what Salivan said in one of his posts:

-There is no engulf south unless price has reached its target for long (so target for long means price has reached an UFL) -There is no engulf north unless price has reached its target for short (so target for short means price has reached a LFL)

Hello Astrokillah, this is repeated by many RTM Masters in different way of writing and Ifmyante in his webinars. But you really have to listen word by word and think at the same time. It took me a while before I noticed...I think I watched the webinars 5-6 times before I noticed...I am stupid like that hahaha =).

However, here goes.

In the first drawing, PA is made. Why? Because the price has reach its target and ITs are either taking off their position or adding more for further shorts. You will know which happens, once engulf happens.

1. If price engulfs this FL, which was the target, then they will want the next FL below. 2. If price arrives at this FL and then balances and shoots back up and engulfs UFL, then it means, there are no more Supply at the UFL. Therefore price will go to higher Supply level to search for more Sell orders. Once there is no more Supply. what happens is, they need to create the Fake Supply and hide their intention of wanting to Buy, therefore they will make it looks like Sell is going on, enticing sellers and breakout sellers in. Why not? =) They want the best possible price, which is this case is MPL, because that Demand has not been taken yet

In the drawing below, the price has not hit its target yet, therefore ITs are not satisfied. They will want to hit Target, before they make new decision. The risk of trading this kind of setups are, you don't know what will happen to the price as it is still in the space and anything can happen, while they play tricks. In this case, the price can go all the way up to MPL of UFL before hitting their target, CP to their level or shoot straight down to their level, if they suddenly want long. Too many options:D, therefore it will be guess work what they will do...Oh and you will not know if the LFL will hold the price or not in this case

EDIT: Ifmyante stated, that ITs dont care about profit, therefore pay attention on stops:D

تو نقاشی اول PA ساخته شده. چرا؟ چون قیمت به تارگتش رسیده و IT‌ها یا دارن پوزیشن‌شون رو می‌بندن یا برای فروش‌های بیشتر اضافه می‌کنن. وقتی اینگالف رخ می‌ده می‌فهمی کدوم اتفاق افتاده.

1. اگه قیمت این FL رو که تارگت بود اینگالف کنه، پس FL بعدی پایین رو می‌خوان. 2. اگه قیمت به این FL برسه و بعد متعادل بشه و دوباره به بالا شلیک کنه و UFL رو اینگالف کنه، یعنی دیگه عرضه‌ای تو UFL نیست. پس قیمت به سطح عرضهٔ بالاتر می‌ره تا سفارش‌های فروش بیشتری پیدا کنه. وقتی دیگه عرضه‌ای نمونده، کاری که می‌کنن ساختن عرضهٔ جعلیه و پنهان کردن قصدشون برای خریده، پس طوری به نظر می‌رسونن که فروش در حال انجامه، تا فروشنده‌ها و تریدرهای بریک‌اوت فروش رو به دام بندازن. چرا نه؟ =) بهترین قیمت ممکن رو می‌خوان که تو این حالت MPL‌ه، چون اون تقاضا هنوز گرفته نشده.

تو نقاشی پایین، قیمت هنوز به تارگتش نرسیده، پس IT‌ها راضی نیستن. می‌خوان قبل از تصمیم جدید تارگت رو بزنن. ریسک معاملهٔ این نوع ستاپ‌ها اینه که نمی‌دونی به قیمت چه می‌شه چون هنوز تو فضاست و هر اتفاقی می‌تونه بیفته، در حالی که اونا کلک می‌زنن. تو این حالت، قیمت می‌تونه همه‌راه تا MPL تو UFL بره قبل از زدن تارگتشون، یا CP به سطحشون، یا مستقیم به سطحشون شلیک کنه اگه ناگهان خرید بخوان. گزینه‌های زیادی:D، پس حدس‌زدنیه که چی کار می‌کنن… اوه و نمی‌دونی تو این حالت LFL قیمت رو نگه می‌داره یا نه

ویرایش: Ifmyante گفت، IT‌ها به سود اهمیت نمی‌دن، پس به استاپ‌ها توجه کن:D
